text: great here is a more complex ask, maybe, idk how you could do it easily and having to select every step of edges would genuinely blow ass... but alright so i was wondering how do i properly incline this bridge as it curves, and, i think the answer is that at ever rung of the edges for its deck, i need to effectively start at the first row of them, nudge it a tap up, then continue with these selected, and select the next ring, nudge both so that the first one still steps higher than this one, and then continue down the ring, the pain in the ass is that i need to do it strictly on these cut across edges and not on the horizontal ones seen in this screenshot. [Image #1]anyways, how would you do it :? maybe there is just a better approach in general like making the one deck piece, and then saying i want a curve and it to gain this much height across so many pieces ?
resolution: Surveyed the active editor and confirmed it has no bend, spline, array, edge-ring, or grade modifier. Recommended a non-destructive Path Array rather than cumulative manual edge nudging: author one bridge bay or grouped bay, then derive a continuous sequence from segment count, total turn, total rise, and a selectable vertical profile. Each generated bay should map between consecutive path frames so shared end rings coincide without curved-deck wedge gaps, while the output remains ordinary independent grouped parts for piece-level editing and bake-through. Also documented the current manual linear-grade fallback and why it should not become the primary workflow.
